title: When periodSeconds is shorter than processing time, startupProbe is executed twice.
body:
### What happened?

I use startupProbe in the following Deployment. In the startupProbe, it waits for the application to start with `initialDelaySeconds: 50` and then start the warm-up process with `timeoutSeconds: 95`. The warm-up process takes about 40 seconds, and the interval in probe is set to `periodSeconds: 10`.

```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: api
spec:
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      run: api
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        run: api
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: api
          image: <IMAGE> # Actually, it is an application image.
         resources:
            limits:
              cpu: "500m"
              memory: "800Mi"
          readinessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /health-check
              port: 8080
            initialDelaySeconds: 0
            periodSeconds: 10
            timeoutSeconds: 4
            successThreshold: 1
            failureThreshold: 3
          livenessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /liveness
              port: 8080
            initialDelaySeconds: 0
            periodSeconds: 10
            timeoutSeconds: 4
            successThreshold: 1
            failureThreshold: 3
          lifecycle:
            preStop:
              exec:
                command: ["sh", "-c", "sleep 20"]
      restartPolicy: Always
      terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 30
      startupProbe:
        exec:
          command:
            - sh
            - -c
            - |
              echo "$(date) startupProbe start" >> /tmp/startupProbe-check
              if [ ! $(curl -s -w "%{http_code}\n" "http://localhost:8080/health-check" -o /dev/null) -eq 200 ]; then
                echo "$(date) startupProbe failed" >> /tmp/startupProbe-check
                exit 1
              fi
              echo "$(date) startupProbe warmup-start" >> /tmp/startupProbe-check
              curl "http://localhost:8080/<API_PATH>"
              sleep 40 # Actually, it is a warmup process.
          echo "$(date) startupProbe warmup-end" >> /tmp/startupProbe-check
        initialDelaySeconds: 0
        periodSeconds: 100
        timeoutSeconds: 100
        successThreshold: 1
        failureThreshold: 1
```

When I run this Deployment, it waits for the application to start for `initialDelaySeconds` as expected. Immediately after that, the first probe begins and succeeds. The `successThreshold` is set to `1`, and since the first probe succeeded, I thought that `startupProbe` ended there, but immediately after the first probe succeeded, the second probe started.

Is this because the `periodSeconds` is too short for the processing time of `exec`, so the second probe is waiting, and it is executed regardless of the success or failure of the first one?

### What did you expect to happen?

Even if the `periodSeconds` is too short for the processing time of `exec` and the second probe has been waiting, I want to make sure that the second probe does not run with the result of the last one.


### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

You can use the following yaml, and check the log `/tmp/startupProbe-check` in the container to see that the second probe is running immediately after the first probe.

```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: startup-probe-research
spec:
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      run: startup-probe-research
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        run: startup-probe-research
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: startup-probe-research
          image: nginx # Actually, it is an application image.
          startupProbe:
            exec:
              command:
                - sh
                - -c
                - |
                  echo "$(date) startupProbe start" >> /tmp/startupProbe-check
                  if [ ! $(curl -s -w "%{http_code}\n" "http://localhost:80/" -o /dev/null) -eq 200 ]; then
                    echo "$(date) startupProbe failed" >> /tmp/startupProbe-check
                    exit 1
                  fi
                  echo "$(date) startupProbe warmup-start" >> /tmp/startupProbe-check
                  curl "http://localhost:80/"
                  sleep 40 # Actually, it is a warmup process.
                  echo "$(date) startupProbe warmup-end" >> /tmp/startupProbe-check
            initialDelaySeconds: 50
            periodSeconds: 10
            timeoutSeconds: 95
            successThreshold: 1
            failureThreshold: 10
```

### Anything else we need to know?

If you increase the `periodSeconds` to `100` seconds, the second probe will not be executed as expected.
However, if `initialDelaySeconds` is shorter than `periodSeconds`, `initialDelaySeconds` becomes meaningless and the application will wait `100` seconds for the first probe. This means that even if the application is started, there will be time wasted waiting for the first probe to be executed.


### Kubernetes version

<details>
 
It happens in both AWS and Docker Deskop.
 
AWS

nodes.title: Stop StartupProbe explicity when successThrethold is reached
nodes.body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind bug

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

`StartupProbe` is executed while container is starting and will update container status to `Started=true` if it succeeds.
When container status becomes to `Started=true`, `StartupProbe` will be stopped and Readiness/Liveness probe will be executed.
Probe and the main loop of kubelet that updates the container status are executed asynchronously, and the goroutine of the Probe requests the container status update to the main loop of kubelet via the channel.
Due to this asyncronicity, `StartupProbe` may be executed more than `successThrethold`.(#117153)

In this PR, `StartupProbe` is stopped explicity when `successThrethold` is reached.


#### Which issue(s) this PR fixes:

Fixes #117153

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?

```release-note
`StartupProbe` is stopped explicity when `successThrethold` is reached. 
This eliminates the problem that `StartupProbe` is executed more than `successThrethold`.
```

title: NodeExpandVolume gets called, even if CSI plugin returned NodeExpansionRequired=false in ControllerExpandVolumeResponse
body:
### What happened?

In case of online volume expansion of raw block volumes, some of the CSI plugins may not need file system resize or any related handling and thus NodeExpandVolume API call can be skipped for the same. In order to do this, plugin must set NodeExpansionRequired to false, in ControllerExpandVolumeResponse.
However, it is observed that kubelet does call NodeExpandVolume API, after successful resize done by CSI plugin in ControllerExpandVolume API call with NodeExpansionRequired=false in response.
Even though CSI plugin can skip handling in NodeExpandVolume API as per its requirement, is it expected to get this API call from kubelet when NodeExpansionRequired set to false by plugin in ControllerExpandVolumeResponse?

### What did you expect to happen?

During CSI volume online expansion, if CSI plugin returns NodeExpansionRequired=false in ControllerExpandVolumeResponse, to indicate no FS resize handling needed, then kubelet should not call NodeExpandVolume API for such volume(s).

title: kubelet: memorymanager  static policy startup error
body:
### What happened?

In our scenario, memoryManager are enabled. There are two numa nodes: node0 and node1 on the host.
The relevant parameter values are as follows：
memoryManagerPolicy: Static

Initially, no pods are running on this node  with two numa node,  220G memory per numa node. Follow the steps bellow to create and delete pods:
1. create guaranteed Pod1 with one container,  memory req and limit: 240G
2. create guaranteed Pod2 with one container, memory req and limit: 20G
At this point, machineState is as follows:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/22569211/196362536-fdc55b24-2246-453b-aa1f-5a5d8533c720.png)

3. delete Pod2
At this point, machineState will be as follows:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/22569211/196362769-283a35ff-b7eb-4ad9-8560-9ac35486dd70.png)


4. create guaranteed Pod3 with one container, memory req and limit: 10G
At this point, actual machineState is as follows:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/22569211/196363134-fc5af58b-32a2-464a-9f6a-7f5ca557bdfd.png)

Now, restarting kubelet will fail. When kubelet restart, the expected machineState is as follows that is not equal to actual machineState above.
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/22569211/196363931-14f8bffa-cf79-48a3-9a0b-3e1b08358ee3.png)







### What did you expect to happen?

Pod creation and deletion order should not cause kubelet restart to fail.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

See analysis above.

### Anything else we need to know?

_No response_

### Kubernetes version

v1.21 and above versions have this problem

None
</details>

nodes.body: /sig node

/triage needs-information

thank you for beautifully crafted error report!!!

The k8s version you are running is old and out of support (kubelet v1.21.0). Would it be possible to check the behavior on latest version of k8s?

I know that there is an existing limitation around cpu manager (not sure about memory manager) that requires to handle checkpoint file before the restart. Not sure if this applies here. Please check on latest k8s and report back.

Thanks for you reply. 

> /triage needs-information
> 
> thank you for beautifully crafted error report!!!
> 
> The k8s version you are running is old and out of support (kubelet v1.21.0). Would it be possible to check the behavior on latest version of k8s?
> 
> I know that there is an existing limitation around cpu manager (not sure about memory manager) that requires to handle checkpoint file before the restart. Not sure if this applies here. Please check on latest k8s and report back.

Thanks for your reply.   I have confirmed that the latest version kubelet has this problem, too.    
When kubelet start ,  static policy of memorymanager will validate the checkpoint file, the verification logic is as follows:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/22569211/196850382-3f1fe0ee-fd60-4ebc-8975-60b016cf5feb.png)

b.NUMAAffinity on line 563 is in ascending order.  That is to say,   when the func validateState generates expectedMachineState,  it always allocate memory from the lowest numa node first, regardless of the current memory allocation of containers.  That will lead to that the actual machineState is not equal to the calculated one.

@SergeyKanzhelev 
Follow the above process, this problem is easy to reproduce. I reproduced the problem on version 1.25.3. 
There is logic flaws in memorymanager of kubelet, which causes the kubelet to fail to restart.
The result is as follows:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/22569211/199643450-70f39047-0f08-4579-ac4c-7bd7381304b9.png)

/cc
I'm interested in this issue

Hmm in general the memory manager should not allow allocating the same NUMA nodes for cross and single NUMA node allocations it is one of the limitations that we have, see https://kubernetes.io/blog/2021/08/11/kubernetes-1-22-feature-memory-manager-moves-to-beta/#single-vs-cross-numa-node-allocation. @gaohuatao-1 Which topology manager do you use?

> Hmm in general the memory manager should not allow allocating the same NUMA nodes for cross and single NUMA node allocations it is one of the limitations that we have, see https://kubernetes.io/blog/2021/08/11/kubernetes-1-22-feature-memory-manager-moves-to-beta/#single-vs-cross-numa-node-allocation. @gaohuatao-1 Which topology manager do you use?

Thanks for your comment.
Using the default topology manager policy: none. In the above example, there is no pod with single NUMA node.

I see, probably it will not be a problem when we will have both pods to be pinned to multiple NUMA nodes. And looks like you are correct under the comment https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/113130#issuecomment-1301607606, we should validate the state in descending order.
BTW kudos for the report :)
@gaohuatao-1  I had a similar problem and I submitted a PR to fix it, Can you help review the code?
For a node group, we cannot restore the free and reserved size of each node in the group after multiple allocations and releases of one resource.
In the third step, is the ideal case that numa1 equals 220 and numa2 equals 20? @gaohuatao-1

> 1. nteed Pod1 with one container

Yes, you are right.

Thanks for your work, I will review it later.

title: [FG:InPlacePodVerticalScaling] Pod Resize - long delay in updating `apiPodStatus.Resources`
body:
### What would you like to be added?

This is really a bug. 

Running pod resize E2E tests full scope in GKE 1-master 1-worker setup takes significantly longer (869s vs 2988s  to run all 34 E2E tests) Initial investigation shows the the issue is NOT in containerd response to ContainerStatus() CRI API that is called within 50 millisec of UpdateContainerResources(). The long delay is in updating apiPodStatus.


### Why is this needed?

There is no good reason I can think of why it should take several 10s of seconds to update the apiPodStatus.Resources.

nodes.body: /sig node

@vinaykul I figure out the problem in our internal version the major reason is the cgroup update and reconcile are separate loops. The first reconcile loop after the update can not retrieve the up-to-date status. This leads a problem that it has to rely on kubelet `—sync-frequency` (default 60s) to sync the pod and then update the status. I can help commit the improvement
/assign @Jeffwan

@vinaykul I try to understand the source of the performance data.  `869s vs 2988s` this is the before/after from prow job   pull-kubernetes-e2e-gce-ubuntu-containerd?  test `Kubernetes e2e suite: [It] [sig-node] Pod InPlace Resize Container [Feature:InPlacePodVerticalScaling]`

Or you run the e2e test individually in your own environment?

The 2988s run time comes for the additional time it takes across all the 30+ different E2E test cases when full E2E testing is enabled. (Disable isFeatureGatePostAlpha() check which runs the test in full-E2E mode where it checks for ContainerStatus.Resources == ContainerSpec.Resources - this requires containerd support. I tested it by replacing the containerd binaries with those I build from latest containerd master)
